# Program review: the 2026-08 campaign {#sec-program-review-2026-08}

::: {.callout-note title="What this chapter is"}
This chapter is the authoritative synthesis of the research program as of
2026-08-24. It supersedes the earlier "future directions" chapter (whose open
questions have all since been measured) and compresses roughly sixty
preregistered training runs, four adversarial probes, and three architecture
generations into the tables and verdicts a reviewer actually needs. Every
number is computed live from the committed reduction artifacts in
`results/`, and every claim links to the dated lab-notebook entry
(@sec-notebook) where it was preregistered and read out. The campaign
narrative (@sec-review-arc) ends 2026-08-19; the refutation wave that
followed (@sec-review-refutation-wave) resolved every mechanism candidate
then open and is the current state of the mechanism hunt. The live
tech-tree ledger is @sec-tech-tree.
:::

## The one-paragraph verdict

The program set out to build a boundary-driven-PDE surrogate whose
generalization comes from **declared physical structure** rather than data
coverage. After a falsification campaign against the strongest available baseline (GeoTransolver, a soft-slice global-attention architecture), the
result is a *decomposition*: *accuracy* at industrial scale comes
from normalized global routing and rich features, and GeoTransolver had it;
*pose robustness* comes from exact equivariance, GeoTransolver measurably
lacks it, and recovering it with data augmentation costs 1.8--1.9$\times$
accuracy where our contracts provide it free; *cross-family transfer* comes
from training-data diversity, not from any architecture we tested; and
*query-independence* — the ability to evaluate the surrogate anywhere without
the answer depending on which other points are sampled — trades directly
against accuracy in every design we built. The program's product is
`MeshTransformer2` (MT2): GeoTransolver's routing wrapped in exact contracts
at the network's edges, within 10--18% of GeoTransolver's in-family accuracy
at equal-or-lower cost, exactly pose-robust, and transferring at parity when
trained on two families.

## The frozen instrument {#sec-review-instrument}

Every comparison in this chapter runs on one instrument, frozen on
2026-08-04 and never widened retroactively: DrivAerML surface pressure at
10,000-cell sampling (in-family), a five-resolution sweep (2.5k--40k cells),
zero-shot evaluation on two held-out SHIFT-SUV vehicle families (estate and
fastback, normalized pressure $L_2$ from the fleet-comparable
`metrics.jsonl` pathway), and — added mid-campaign as adversarial probes —
a full random-yaw rotation orbit (P1), a drive-amplitude scaling ladder
(P2), a 10:1 spatially-biased sampling density with exact
Horvitz--Thompson weights (P3), and a shared-prefix companion-set stability
test (P4). Training protocol is identical for every arm ever compared: 500
epochs, batch 1, lr $3\times10^{-3}$ StepLR, bfloat16, no augmentation
unless the augmentation *is* the arm, four-GPU single-node DDP on identical
hardware. A two-point learning-rate parity check ran for both architectures;
it moves the headline gap from 1.18$\times$ to 1.10$\times$ in MT2's favor
and is reported wherever it matters.

## The frontier, in one table {#sec-review-frontier}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-frontier
#| output: asis
#| code-fold: true
import json
from pathlib import Path

R = Path("..") / "results" / "mixedres_training_2026-07-31" / "sweep"
mega = json.load(open(R / "mega_reduction.json"))
round3 = json.load(open(R / "round3_reduction.json"))
v3c = json.load(open(R / "mt2_v3c_reduction.json"))

def mean(vals):
    return sum(vals) / len(vals)

gt10 = mean([round3[f"gt_fixed_seed{s}"]["sweep_metrics"]["10000"]["mean"]
             for s in (42, 43, 44)])
gt_zs = mean([round3[f"gt_fixed_seed{s}"]["smoke_estate"]["mean"]
              for s in (42, 43, 44)])

rot_in = mean([mega[f"gt_rotaug_seed{s}"]["in10k"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43)])
rot_zs = mean([mega[f"gt_rotaug_seed{s}"]["estate"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43)])

v3c_in = mean(
    [v3c[f"mt2_v3c_seed{s}"]["sweep"]["10000"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)]
    + [mega[f"mt2_v3c_seed{s}"]["in10k"]["mean"] for s in (45, 46)]
)
v3c_zs = mean([v3c[f"mt2_v3c_seed{s}"]["smoke_estate"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)])

mt2m_in = mean([mega[f"mt2_multi_seed{s}"]["in10k"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)])
mt2m_zs = mean([mega[f"mt2_multi_seed{s}"]["fastback"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)])
gtm_in = mean([mega[f"gt_multi_seed{s}"]["in10k"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)])
gtm_zs = mean([mega[f"gt_multi_seed{s}"]["fastback"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)])

rows = [
    ("GeoTransolver 9M", 1.0, gt_zs, "3.6x", "26-32x broken", "4.6 GB",
     "GeoTransolver reference"),
    ("GT + rotation aug.", rot_in / gt10, rot_zs, "--", "closed (1.00)",
     "4.6 GB", "the augmentation price"),
    ("MT2-v3c (8.6M)", v3c_in / gt10, v3c_zs, "13-14x", "exact (1.00)",
     "5.9 GB", "canonical single-family MT2"),
    ("GT multi-family", gtm_in / gt10, gtm_zs, "--", "26-32x broken",
     "4.6 GB", "zero-shot on HELD-OUT family"),
    ("MT2 multi-family", mt2m_in / gt10, mt2m_zs, "--", "exact (1.00)",
     "5.9 GB", "zero-shot on HELD-OUT family"),
]
out = ("| configuration | in-family (xGT) | zero-shot | density (P3) "
       "| rotation (P1) | peak VRAM | note |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n")
for (n, i, z, d, r_, m, note) in rows:
    out += f"| {n} | {i:.2f}x | {z:.2f} | {d} | {r_} | {m} | {note} |\n"
print(out)
print(f": The frontier on the frozen instrument. In-family is normalized "
      f"pressure $L_2$ at 10k cells relative to the GeoTransolver reference "
      f"({gt10:.4f}); zero-shot is the mean normalized pressure $L_2$ on a "
      f"held-out vehicle family (estate for single-family rows, fastback "
      f"for the multi-family rows; 1.0 is mean-predictor level). Sources: "
      f"mega_reduction.json, round3_reduction.json, mt2_v3c_reduction.json.")
```

Three facts to read off the table before any narrative. First, **the
augmentation price**: closing GeoTransolver's rotation hole with the classic
data-augmentation remedy costs it most of its accuracy lead —
1.8--1.9$\times$ in-family — while MT2's exact equivariance is free by
construction; at equal pose-robustness the structured model is the
*more* accurate one by roughly 1.6$\times$. Second, **the multi-family rows are a
coverage result, not generalization** (reframed 2026-08-20,
@sec-nb-generalization-northstar): one additional training family moves
held-out-family error from mean-predictor level to 0.11--0.13 for *both*
architectures — a $\sim$7$\times$ improvement that dwarfs every
architectural intervention measured on that axis. This shows
that *neither* architecture was extrapolating beyond its training hull.
Measuring generalization — as scaling curves and
beyond-distribution tests rather than points inside an expanded hull — is
the program's current campaign.
Third, **the remaining accuracy gap is small and tuning-sensitive**: 1.18×
at the frozen learning rate, 1.10× when each architecture uses its
preferred rate.

## How we got here: the campaign in five verdicts {#sec-review-arc}

**1. The original MeshTransformer's defects were real, and three closed at root
cause** (@sec-nb-model-quality-agenda ff.). Resolution collapse was a
quadrature-bookkeeping error, cured by measure-consistent
Horvitz--Thompson weighting (@sec-nb-mixedres-verdict). Foreign-family
detonation was the nonlinear read-in's implicit drive degree, removed
exactly by declaring degree one (@sec-nb-bounded-stage1-verdict). Seed
instability collapsed from 2491$\times$ to order-1.3$\times$ as a
byproduct. These closures are the program's clearest demonstrations that
mechanism-first debugging beats remedy-first patching.

**2. GeoTransolver comparison was re-anchored with matched controls, and GeoTransolver
won the measured axes** (@sec-nb-incumbent-stage0-verdict,
@sec-nb-defect4-synthesis). At every resource budget tested,
GeoTransolver dominated in-family accuracy, zero-shot transfer, density
robustness, and training cost — including a resource re-framing
(@sec-nb-resource-accounting) that showed the original matched-*parameter*
comparison had flattered our side. The synthesis recommended inverting the
program: structure the winner rather than accelerate the loser.

**3. The probes made the benchmark's blind spots measurable**
(@sec-nb-contract-probes-synthesis). Rotation: GeoTransolver loses
26--32$\times$ off-pose — every number it posts carries an implicit "in
the dataset's canonical pose." Amplitude: its output is drive-amplitude
*blind* (layer normalization saturates scale), while the declared-degree
contract measures exactly 1.0000. Density: geometry-adaptive statistics
pay a variance-bounded tax no weighting scheme removes; the measure
contract halves the damage but cannot zero it.

**4. MT2 was built in eleven preregistered iterations, most of which
failed informatively** (@sec-nb-mt2-charter through
@sec-nb-v5-line-verdict). The thesis — GeoTransolver's routing on
exclusively invariant features, contracts paid once at the network edges —
was refuted at v0 (non-separating invariants), remained viable at v0b, shed its
global frames entirely at v2 on Peter's correction that no canonical frame
exists in the physics, and closed its in-family gap by featurization alone
(3.08$\times \to$ 1.15$\times$; capacity was flat at every rung tested).
The accuracy--robustness trade that emerged was then shown to be a
*single-family-training artifact*, dissolved by data diversity rather than
architecture.

**5. Query-independence was priced, and the price is the finding**
(@sec-nb-v5-line-verdict). Three passive-decoder designs either collapsed
in training or, once the collapse was fixed by a local token readout,
converged 2.7$\times$ worse in-family while achieving the best density
robustness of any variant. Conclusion, now measured rather than argued:
**in this design family, accuracy and query-interaction are entangled** —
the query-side token stream is where the accuracy comes from, which is
also precisely why the accurate models carry companion-set sensitivity
(2% for GeoTransolver, 6.8% for MT2-v3c on the P4 probe). A deployable
surrogate can have exact evaluate-anywhere semantics at 3.9$\times$ the
error, or near-GeoTransolver accuracy with single-digit-percent sensitivity;
it cannot currently have both.

## The refutation wave: every open mechanism candidate, resolved {#sec-review-refutation-wave}

The G1/G2 scaling ladder (@sec-nb-g1g2-verdict) gave the mechanism hunt
its target: **the G2 transfer gap** — GeoTransolver's zero-shot error on
a held-out vehicle family improves monotonically with in-family training
data (0.784 → 0.657 across five training-set-size rungs) while
MeshTransformer2's stays flat at 0.83–0.94. Between 2026-08-20 and
2026-08-21, five preregistered lines resolved every candidate
explanation then on the table. None of these are open questions anymore;
each verdict below is dated and anchored.

**Locality: refuted as the transfer carrier** (@sec-nb-locality-verdict).
The hypothesis that GeoTransolver's transfer compounding is carried by
local features predicted that MeshTransformer2's flag-gated local
patch-integral channel would bend MT2's G2 curve downward. Measured: the
local channel yields a consistent but *constant* 3–5% in-family improvement
(the ratio to plain MT2 rises 0.953 → 0.972 across rungs — an offset,
not a slope change), does not improve zero-shot transfer, and
*destabilizes* it at the largest rung (n=218 seed spread 0.12 vs 0.02
in-family). The channel remains an MT3 candidate only as a cheap in-family
offset.

**The literature wave: all four arms resolved one day after
preregistration** (prereg 69a81e2a, @sec-nb-lit-wave-prereg;
wave-close @sec-nb-m1-verdict-wave-close):

- **M1 scale relaxation: REFUTED** (@sec-nb-m1-verdict-wave-close).
  Appending a log raw-cloud-radius scalar — breaking MT2's
  exact scale equivariance — gained only 1.3–2.0% in-family, inside the
  declared ±3% seed band and far from the preregistered >5% threshold,
  and *hurt* zero-shot transfer (0.949–0.956 vs plain MT2's
  0.825–0.856). Caveat preserved: DrivAerML's scale signal is weak
  (fixed freestream); the Reynolds-varying high-lift wave is the strong
  test.
- **M2 anchor-conditioned decode: CLOSED at the pilot gate**
  (@sec-nb-v5a4-gate). The AB-UPT-style design (a fixed 2,560-token
  interacting anchor core, all queries decoding passively) came in at
  0.01517 against the preregistered 0.01500 bar — a fail by 1.2%; no
  seeds promoted. The query-independence price finding of
  @sec-nb-v5-line-verdict stands; any reopening requires a new
  matched-resource preregistration, not a rerun.
- **M3 invariant completeness: PARTIAL** (@sec-nb-m3-verdict). An
  expressivity ceiling is real — geometries with a discrete rotational
  symmetry about the drive axis are provably invisible to MT2's
  invariant set — but it is refuted as a DrivAerML-scale limitation (no
  car has such a symmetry; 1° of drive misalignment restores
  separation). The audit's by-product was finding and **fixing a   reflection-equivariance defect in MT2's vector head** (the `parity_fix`
  flag; see @sec-mt2-architecture).
- **M4 NEO normalization audit: CLOSED BY DERIVATION**
  (@sec-nb-lit-wave-prereg). MT2 was already measure-complete — measure
  weights enter every point-population normalization — so the P3
  density floor (4.3–4.5× at 10:1 bias) is the information-limited
  component the importance-sampling analysis predicts, not a bug. No
  retrain arm was warranted.

**G3, the boundary-condition axis: contracts guarantee only what they
declare, and no tested mechanism improves frequency coverage** (@sec-nb-g3-verdict).
On the exact-label 2D conformal-Laplace suite (three arms at matched
parameters: MeshTransformer2 with a boundary-scalar channel, the
soft-slice mechanism of GeoTransolver's family, and MeshTransformer in
drive-linear mode), the drive-linearity contract makes amplitude
extrapolation *free* — exact at ×2 and ×4 amplitude — while the two
learned-amplitude arms degrade 6–12× (MT2+BC-scalar) and 4.5–7×
(soft-slice): the first measured price of an undeclared linearity. But
*no* arm generalizes across BC frequency content: on drive modes never
seen in training, every architecture reaches rel-L2 ≈ 1.0–1.2, as bad
as predicting zero — a data-coverage limit no tested mechanism
addresses. MT2+BC-scalar wins absolute error on every axis (1.8× better
than soft-slice at control) but has the *worst* amplitude degradation
ratio; architecture-driven BC generalization, as preregistered, was not
observed.

**What remains.** With locality refuted, the scale axis refuted, the
expressivity ceiling ruled out at DrivAerML scale, and the normalization
audit closed, the remaining candidate mechanisms for the G2 transfer
gap are GeoTransolver's **pointwise raw coordinate features** and its
**non-equivariant global encoder** — the hypothesis that transfer on
this instrument is carried by representations exact similarity
equivariance forbids MT2 from learning. The corresponding qualification is
that the same equivariance provides MT2's free pose robustness and small-data
parity. The discriminators in flight: the **high-lift wave**
(GeoTransolver vs MeshTransformer2 on the HiLiftAeroML curated full
split, ~epoch 260 of 500 as of 2026-08-24) and, gated on its readout,
the **HiLift generalization ladder**. Mid-flight, both GeoTransolver
seeds destabilized at the frozen lr 3e-3 (tuned on DrivAerML, where an
epoch is 54 optimizer steps; HiLift's is 315), so an lr-parity
amendment was preregistered *before any readout exists*: symmetric
lr-1e-3 lanes for both architectures under the steel-man rule, each
architecture reporting its best lane over {3e-3, 1e-3}
(@sec-nb-hl-lr-amendment).

## What this does not solve {#sec-review-honesty}

The claims above are scoped by construction, and the scoping is part of
the result. The industrial evidence rests on two automotive dataset
families plus a harder third (high-lift) in flight; no volume fields.
Boundary-condition variation is now measured, but only in 2D with exact
labels (the G3 suite, @sec-nb-g3-verdict); its verdict — amplitude
generalization is purchasable by a declared linearity contract at a
measured 4.5--12$\times$ value, frequency-content generalization is
purchasable by nothing tested — is what any 3D BC-varying dataset
decision should be built on. The typed-BC ingestion that distinguishes
the GLOBE lineage remains unbuilt at industrial scale for the same
reason as before: no *industrial* benchmark can yet measure it.
Density robustness is scoped at $\sim$13$\times$ under a 10:1 sampling
bias — and the M4 audit closed the question of whether that floor is a
normalization bug: MeshTransformer2 is already measure-complete, so the
floor is information-limited (@sec-nb-lit-wave-prereg). Both
architectures misbehave at scale extremes
under the frozen learning rate (seed-conditioned detonations at 11M for
the original MeshTransformer; a turned frontier at 564M for GeoTransolver), so
no "scales to very large runs" claim is made by either side. And the
irreducible-error question — whether the 1.10$\times$ residual gap is
architecture or the dataset's time-averaging noise floor — is exactly
what the running high-lift wave (@sec-nb-highlift-prereg) exists to
answer, now under its preregistered lr-parity amendment
(@sec-nb-hl-lr-amendment).

## Roads from here {#sec-review-roads}

In recommended order: (1) a scoped experimental release of MT2-v3c/v4 —
"exactly pose-robust surface aero surrogate at GeoTransolver-class accuracy
and cost," with the augmentation pricing as its headline evidence and the
entanglement finding as its stated limitation; (2) the high-lift verdict
(running, @sec-nb-hl-lr-amendment), which either extends the claim to
harder physics or bounds it, and which gates the two planned nodes of
the tech tree (@sec-tech-tree): the HiLift generalization ladder — the
Reynolds-varying analogue of the G1/G2 ladder, the strongest remaining
discriminator for the surviving G2-gap candidates — and the MT3
preregistration; (3) the
upstream PR series for the engineering bycatch (rank-failure barrier,
distributed-timeout knob, degenerate-cell guards, measure infrastructure — all
verified still absent upstream); (4) any 3D BC-varying dataset decision,
now informed by the completed 2D G3 fingerprint (@sec-nb-g3-verdict):
build it for the axes where architecture can matter — amplitude and
geometry — because frequency-content coverage is a data axis no tested
mechanism improves; and (5) the closed query-independence line — the fully
passive decode priced at 2.7$\times$ (@sec-nb-v5-line-verdict) and the
anchor-conditioned variant closed at its pilot gate
(@sec-nb-v5a4-gate) — revisited only via the registered follow-up (a
matched-resource anchor-count scaling study under a new
preregistration) and only if a deployment actually demands
evaluate-anywhere semantics at the measured price.
